newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES QUOTED MIXED ON FRIDAY.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES QUOTED MIXED ON FRIDAY.

text.p: HARARE, June 6 (Reutetr) - Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted mixed on Friday, dealers said.

The market opened with a slight surplus of Z$9.6 million but the central Reserve Bank forecast a Z$23 million shortage at the end of the day, for which reason it was not auctioning any treasury bills as it normally does to mop up excess liquidity.
On the secondary market, treasury bills were being traded at 22.75 percent, slightly down from 23 percent but call money edged up to 23 percent from 22.
NCD bills redeemable after 30, 60 and 90 days were being bought at 27 percent from 25.5 percent while their selling rate eased to 23.5 from 24.5 percent.
Bank acceptance bills were quoted at 26 percent percent (buying) from 24.5 and were being sold steadily at 23 percent.
